files.aging-report-prc-114.md:
---
name: aging-report-prc-114
description: PRC-114 aging_report() in parcelo/reports.py (buckets 0-30 / 31-60 / 60+ on open invoices). APPROVED first pass (CI passed, review approved). Read for any aging / age-bucket / days-outstanding report ticket.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Outcome: implemented 2026-11-12. CI passed and code review approved on the first pass. No CI-only tests, no requested changes.

Files: `aging_report()` and helper `_as_utc()` in `parcelo/reports.py`; 7 tests in `tests/unit/test_aging_report.py` (new file, per [[review-feedback-test-placement]]); CHANGELOG line `- [PRC-114] reports: invoice aging report ...` under Unreleased.

Decisions that were approved (reuse for similar report tickets):
- Open only: `status == "open"` (matches `invoices.open_invoices()`). Paid skipped.
- Age = `(clock.now() - issued_at).days`, whole days, clamped at 0 for future-dated invoices. Buckets: `<=30` "0-30", `<=60` "31-60", else "60+".
- Totals are `Money`, starting from `Money.zero()`, adding `Money.parse(invoice.amount)`. Empty bucket = `Money.zero()`.
- `issued_at` is naive UTC in this tree. The PRC-114 helper `_as_utc()` lives in `reports.py` and treats naive values as UTC before subtracting.
- `issued_at is None` on an open invoice -> `DomainError("E_BAD_STATE")`. Chosen over silently dropping money from a finance report; the ticket was silent on this.
- Ticket pointed at legacy `days_between` in `parcelo/legacy/billing.py`. It was NOT imported (legacy ban, see [[parcelo-conventions]]). The one-line arithmetic was reimplemented inline. Approved. Same pattern as [[legacy-reimplementation]].
- Tests cover: empty report is all zero; bucket boundaries (0, 30, 31, 60, 61 days); paid excluded; 30 days 23 hours counts as 30 whole days; naive `issued_at` treated as UTC; result is a `Money` instance; report does not mutate invoices.

Stale-note correction: earlier memories say `invoices._as_utc()` and `late_fee_for` (PRC-106) exist in `invoices.py`. The PRC-114 session did not find `_as_utc` in `invoices.py` and wrote its own copy in `reports.py`. Grep before reusing either helper.

See [[reports-outstanding-prc-108]] (Money-in-reports pattern), [[invoice-timestamps]], [[ticket-checklist]].
files.claims-prc-112.md:
---
name: claims-prc-112
description: PRC-112 file_claim(shipment_id, amount, reason) in parcelo/claims.py. CHANGES REQUESTED + CI FAILED (delivered guard required delivered_at, which nothing sets). Read for any "file / submit / open X on a shipment" ticket.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Outcome: NOT approved. CI failed on two hidden tests, and review requested changes. Local suite was green (24 passed: 5 baseline + 19 in `tests/unit/test_file_claim.py`), which hid the bug.

**CI failure (the real bug):** `test_file_claim_stores_claim` and `test_claims_get_distinct_ids` both raised `E_BAD_STATE: shipment shp_000001 is not delivered (status=delivered)`. The hidden tests set `status="delivered"` and did NOT set `delivered_at`. My guard was `status != "delivered" or delivered_at is None`, so it rejected them.
- Why I wrote it: I copied the "check status AND timestamp" rule from [[state-transitions]].
- Why it was wrong: `delivered_at` is never written anywhere in the tree (`shipments.mark_delivered` does not exist, see [[parcelo-conventions]]). So the guard could only pass in tests that set it by hand. The ticket defines delivered as the status only.
- Fix: guard on `shipment.status == "delivered"` only. Drop the `delivered_at` check.
- Test fix: add a test where status is "delivered" and `delivered_at` is None, expecting success. Keep the status-only path pinned.

**Review comments (received on this ticket):**
- Audit missing on the stored change.
- Use `clock.now()`, not `datetime.now()`/`utcnow()`.
- Use `ids.new_id("<prefix>")`, not uuid.
- Return `Money`, not float.

Caveat: the submitted diff already had all four. `audit.record("claim.filed", ...)`, `clock.now()`, `ids.new_id("clm")`, and `Money.parse` were all present. So either the reviewer read different code or the comments were generic. Before the next submit, check each comment against the code with file:line and state in the final message which lines satisfy it. Do not rewrite working code to match a comment that is already met. See [[review-rules-prc-103]].

**Pattern as implemented (keep, except the state guard):**
- Lookup via `shipments.get_shipment` first -> `E_NOT_FOUND`.
- Amount: `Money.parse`. Parse failure (ArithmeticError/TypeError/ValueError) or cents <= 0 -> `E_BAD_INPUT`. Covers None, "abc", NaN, "0", "-3".
- Reason: non-str or blank -> `E_BAD_INPUT`. The ticket's "anything else must fail" was read to include this.
- State: `status != "delivered"` -> `E_BAD_STATE`. (Corrected; see above.)
- Id: `ids.new_id("clm")`.
- `filed_at = clock.now()`. Audit `claim.filed` with `shipment_id` in details. Failed calls write no audit and store nothing.
- Changelog line: `- [PRC-112] claims: file claims on delivered shipments`.

**Lessons (general, also in [[ticket-checklist]]):**
- Don't add a guard the ticket doesn't state. For each guard, grep for the code that writes that field. If nothing writes it, the guard cannot be satisfied through the real API, so don't use it.
- My own tests set both fields, so they couldn't catch an over-strict guard. Test each condition on its own: a status-only setup must pass.
- CI runs hidden tests with minimal setup. Write setups that match the ticket's wording, not a fuller setup.

Related: [[state-transitions]], [[shipment-notes-prc-111]], [[ticket-checklist]], [[parcelo-conventions]].

files.customer-credit-limit-prc-150.md:
---
name: customer-credit-limit-prc-150
description: PRC-150 set_credit_limit(customer_id, amount) in parcelo/customers.py. CHANGES REQUESTED: reviewer rejected the float write-back to Customer.credit_limit (must use Money). Unknown customer -> E_NOT_FOUND, negative/None -> E_BAD_INPUT, events.emit customer.credit_limit_set. Read for any "change a customer setting / limit" ticket.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Outcome: CHANGES REQUESTED (feedback received 2026-11-12). CI passed. Reviewer: "This returns a raw float for a currency amount. New code has to use `Money` from `parcelo.money` (wrap older float values with `Money.parse`). We stopped passing floats around for money after the rounding incident."

What I submitted: 7 tests in `tests/unit/test_set_credit_limit.py`, `set_credit_limit` returns `Money`, and it stores `customer.credit_limit = limit.cents / 100` (a float) with a comment citing the PRC-113 float precedent. The reviewer rejected the float write-back. The PRC-113 precedent is NOT a safe excuse (see [[invoice-credit-prc-113]]).

Lesson: any new code that writes a money value into a float field is a finding, even if the field is declared `float` and a neighbouring function does the same. Do not add a comment that justifies the float; fix it. Before coding, grep the tree for other readers of the field, then decide whether the field itself should become `Money` (with a default that keeps existing constructors working, per [[ticket-checklist]] step 5). If the field change is wider than the ticket, say so and ask in the final message rather than silently keep the float.

Pattern that is still valid:
- Guards: `customer_id not in db.customers` -> `E_NOT_FOUND` (checked first, directly on `db.customers`, like [[upgrade-tier-prc-145]]). `amount is None` -> `E_BAD_INPUT` (my addition; ticket silent). `Money.parse(amount) < Money.zero()` -> `E_BAD_INPUT`. Zero is allowed (ticket only bans negatives).
- Event: `events.emit("customer.credit_limit_set", customer_id, credit_limit=str(limit))`. No `audit.record` (see [[events-outbox-replaces-audit]]).
- Error paths emit nothing and leave the limit unchanged (tests check both).
- Changelog line: `- [PRC-150] customers: set customer credit limit`.

Verified in tree: `Customer.credit_limit` is declared `float` (default `500.0`), and nothing else in the tree reads it. `customers.py` has no `deactivate_customer`. `errors.CODES` already has `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_BAD_INPUT`, `E_LIMIT`.

Next time for this ticket family: return `Money` and keep the stored value as Money (or whatever the reviewer names), with no float write-back. Check the review feedback before you rely on any precedent.

See [[ticket-checklist]], [[parcelo-conventions]], [[review-rules-prc-103]].

Pattern used (follows [[state-transitions]], [[review-idempotent-transitions-prc-152]], [[ticket-checklist]]):
- Lookup via `db.customers.get`; `None` -> `DomainError("E_NOT_FOUND")`. `get_customer` is NOT used because it raises a bare `KeyError`.
- Idempotent: already `active` -> return the customer, no event, no write.
- Otherwise set `active = True`, `events.emit("customer.reactivated", customer_id)`, return the customer (same object).
- Docs line in `docs/api.md`, changelog line `- [PRC-154] customers: reactivate customer`.
- Tests: 5 in `tests/unit/test_reactivate_customer.py` (inactive -> active, event emitted, unknown -> E_NOT_FOUND with no event, already active -> no event, repeat call idempotent). The test count was recorded at implementation time and was not re-run in the feedback session.

Scope notes from the approved diff:
- The ticket asked only for the flag change and the not-found error. The idempotent path and the `events.emit` call were added beyond the literal wording. The reviewer accepted both. They match the house conventions ([[events-outbox-replaces-audit]], [[review-idempotent-transitions-prc-152]]), so for future tickets, adding the convention-required event and idempotent return is fine. Don't drop them.
- Stale note: [[parcelo-conventions]] says `customers.deactivate_customer` (PRC-104) and `set_credit_limit` (PRC-150) exist in `customers.py`. Neither was in the tree when I last looked. Check with grep before relying on either.

How to reuse: for any "undo a status change" ticket on a customer, shipment, or invoice, copy this function's shape (lookup with `.get`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, no-op on same state, `events.emit`, same-object return).

name: events-outbox-replaces-audit
description: Since the PRC-140 events outbox, NEW mutations emit via events.emit(name, entity_id, ...) from parcelo/events.py and must NOT call audit.record. Read for any ticket that changes data (create, mutate, reassign, mark, void, add).

Review on PRC-141 (`shipments.reassign_shipment`) requested changes: "We moved off `audit.record` last sprint. New mutations must call `events.emit(name, entity_id, ...)` from `parcelo.events` instead, and must not call `audit.record` directly anymore (the audit log is fed from the outbox)."

The rule for every new mutation:
1. Import `events` from `parcelo` (`from parcelo import events`). Do not import `audit` for the write path.
2. Call `events.emit("<entity>.<action>", entity_id, ...)`, e.g. `events.emit("shipment.reassigned", shipment_id, old_customer_id=..., new_customer_id=...)`. Name and id order follow the reviewer's stated signature. Check `parcelo/events.py` for the exact signature before coding, because I have only the reviewer's description, not the source.
3. Do not call `audit.record` in new code. Existing functions that still call it (PRC-104, 107, 109, 111, 112, 113 and so on) predate the change; don't rewrite them unless the ticket asks.
4. Tests: do not assert on `audit.LOG` for new mutations. Assert on `events.OUTBOX`, a list of dicts with `"name"` and `"entity_id"` keys (confirmed by the approved PRC-145 tests). Call `events.OUTBOX.clear()` before the action, then check `OUTBOX[-1]` or `OUTBOX == []` for the no-event case. See [[upgrade-tier-prc-145]].
5. The `CHANGELOG.md` line already shows `platform: add events outbox (PRC-140)` in the OLD trailing-id form (the current form is `[PRC-140] platform: ...`), so the switch was visible in the changelog. Read the CHANGELOG for "platform" or "events" entries before coding, to catch convention changes like this one.

Why: the audit log is now fed from the outbox. A direct `audit.record` call bypasses that and was rejected in review. My PRC-141 submission used `audit.record` because [[parcelo-conventions]] and [[ticket-checklist]] step 4 both said so. Those notes were stale. I followed the memory instead of checking whether the convention had changed.

How to apply: before writing any mutation, grep the tree for `events.emit` and `audit.record`. If `events.emit` is used by recent code (PRC-140 onward), use it. Update the old notes, and treat any "audit.record" rule in older memory files as superseded for new work. See [[shipment-reassign-prc-141]] and [[state-transitions]].

---
name: legacy-reimplementation
description: How to port a formula from parcelo/legacy/ into new code without importing it (PRC-103 surcharge, PRC-106 late fee). Read when a ticket says "the same formula already exists" or names a legacy function.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Tickets often say a formula "already exists" in `parcelo/legacy/`. Legacy is banned from imports and scheduled for deletion, so the formula must be reimplemented in the new module.

Pattern that worked (PRC-106, `late_fee_for` in `parcelo/invoices.py`):
- Read the legacy function first and write down its inputs, day counting, boundary (is day 30 late?), rounding, and return type.
- Copy only the constants and arithmetic, as module-level constants (e.g. `LATE_AFTER_DAYS`, `LATE_FEE_PER_DAY = Decimal("0.015")`). Do not copy the whole module.
- Use `Money` for the return value and `Decimal` for the rate, not float.
- Add a test per boundary (before, exactly at, one past, several days past) and one type/precision test.

Known gaps and traps:
- PRC-106 tests use hand-computed values. Nothing in the test file compares against legacy output, and no parity check was run. If a ticket says "same as legacy", add a parity test with values taken from the legacy function's output, or flag the gap in the final message.
- PRC-103 (`quote_with_surcharge`): the fuel surcharge percentages live only in legacy `fuel_surcharge`. Copy the percentages into `rates.py`. The return shape was never confirmed, and CI failed with `TypeError: float() ... not 'tuple'`. Check existing callers before choosing a return shape.
- Timestamps: legacy and `issue_invoice` use naive UTC. Normalize before subtracting (grep for an existing `_as_utc`; the PRC-114 session did not find one in `invoices.py`). See [[invoice-timestamps]].
- PRC-114 (`aging_report`): the ticket said `days_between` in legacy "already has the day arithmetic". Reimplemented inline as `(now - issued).days`, no import. Approved first pass. Ticket-named legacy helpers are usually one-liners: write them inline, do not import.

- PRC-144 (`insurance_fee`): the fuel surcharge percents were copied into `rates.py` as a second table. Approved first pass, but the two copies can drift and no parity test was written. When a ticket reuses a legacy table, copy it and note the drift risk in the final message.

- PRC-147 (`volume_report`): tier thresholds copied as constants and approved, but the "matches legacy" test hardcodes the numbers. Parity with `volume_tier` was never run. Still a gap: for "same thresholds as legacy" tickets, read the legacy function (check for extra tiers, e.g. the CHANGELOG "Added gold tier" entry) and state in the final message whether you checked parity.

- Invoice -> customer join via `db.shipments[invoice.shipment_id].customer_id`, open-only, same as [[reports-outstanding-prc-108]].
- Total accumulated as `Money` via `Money.parse(invoice.amount)`. Compare with `<` against the threshold (Money defines `__lt__`/`__le__` only, so use the reflected form, not `>`).
- Read-only: no `events.emit`, no audit. Test asserts `events.OUTBOX == []`.
- Boundaries pinned: exactly 3 invoices False, 4 True; total exactly 250.00 False, 250.01 True.

files.parcelo-conventions.md:
---
name: parcelo-conventions
description: Code conventions for the parcelo repo (errors, money, legacy package ban, events vs audit (events.emit for new code), changelog, test file placement, state checks, clock)
metadata:
  type: project
---

- **Errors:** raise `DomainError(code, msg)` with a code from `parcelo/errors.py` `CODES`; unregistered codes raise RuntimeError. Use `E_NOT_FOUND` for missing entities (via `get_shipment`) and `E_BAD_STATE` for invalid state transitions. If nothing fits, add a new `E_...` code to `CODES`. Never raise bare `ValueError`/`KeyError` in new code, even when a ticket says "must fail" (see [[review-rules-prc-103]]).
- **Money:** currency amounts are `Money` from `parcelo/money.py`, never raw floats. Wrap older float values with `Money.parse`. (Reason: rounding incident; see [[review-rules-prc-103]].) This includes STORED values: do not write `cents / 100` back into a float field to "match the declared type". PRC-150 was rejected for exactly that ([[customer-credit-limit-prc-150]]); the PRC-113 float write-back is not a safe precedent. Existing float-returning helpers (`rates.quote`, `rates.base_rate`) are legacy-style and are NOT a template for new code. Rejected again on PRC-110 ([[rates-gold-discount-prc-110]]).
- **Legacy ban:** never import from `parcelo.legacy` in new code. That package is scheduled for deletion. If you need a small piece of it (e.g. a percentage), reimplement it next to your change. Do not copy the whole module.
- **Mutations emit events (current rule, from PRC-141 review):** new mutations call `events.emit("<entity>.<action>", id, ...)` from `parcelo/events.py`. Do NOT call `audit.record` in new code; the audit log is fed from the outbox (PRC-140). See [[events-outbox-replaces-audit]]. Older functions (e.g. `invoice.voided` in PRC-102, `customer.deactivated`) still call `audit.record`; leave them alone unless the ticket asks.
- **Lists and docs (PRC-151 changes requested):** functions returning lists of entities sort by `id` ascending. Every new public function gets a line in `docs/api.md`. See [[review-list-order-and-docs-prc-151]].
- Each ticket gets a line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md in the bracket-first format: `- [PRC-101] shipments: ...`. The id goes FIRST in square brackets. The old trailing `(PRC-101)` form is rejected (PRC-159 CHANGES REQUESTED; the release script ignores it). See [[review-changelog-format-prc-159]].
- Delivered shipments: "delivered" means `status == "delivered"` (the ticket's definition). `shipments.mark_delivered` is NOT in the tree (shipments.py only has create_shipment and get_shipment), so nothing writes `delivered_at`. Do not require `delivered_at` in guards: PRC-112 failed CI on that. A historical PRC-107 note said mark_delivered was approved; treat that as unverifiable, since the function is absent. Full state-transition pattern and error rules: see [[state-transitions]]. No `cancel_shipment` exists in the tree.
- Hidden CI tests: CI runs tests with names I did not write (PRC-103, PRC-112). Write setups using only what the ticket says (e.g. status only), not extra fields I think are needed.
- Tests: every ticket gets a NEW test file under `tests/unit/` named after the feature (e.g. `tests/unit/test_cancel_shipment.py`). Do NOT add to `tests/unit/test_shipments.py` or any top-level `tests/` file; those are frozen. See [[review-feedback-test-placement]].
- `tests/conftest.py` has an autouse fixture that resets store, ids, audit, clock, so tests need no manual setup.
- No git repo in the working directory. Run the suite with `python -m pytest -q`. Baseline was 5 tests before PRC-101. Recorded counts from past sessions are not reliable: the "9 passing" note after PRC-102 and PRC-105 was never re-verified, and PRC-103 added 9 tests in `tests/unit/test_quote_with_surcharge.py` that CI then failed (see [[review-rules-prc-103]]). Always re-run `python -m pytest -q` and report the output you actually see.
- PRC-104 (`customers.deactivate_customer`): unknown id -> `E_NOT_FOUND`, already inactive -> `E_BAD_STATE`, audit `customer.deactivated`. Tests in `tests/unit/test_deactivate_customer.py`. CI passed and review approved on first pass. Reviewer accepted the audit call even though the ticket did not ask for it: audit every mutation, as the convention says.
- Rates/surcharge: fuel surcharge percentages live only in `parcelo/legacy/billing.py` `fuel_surcharge`. Because of the legacy ban, copy the percentages into `rates.py` (or the new module) instead of importing them. Check the ticket and existing callers for the expected return shape before you pick one. For PRC-103 the tuple `(base, surcharge)` was never confirmed, and CI hit `TypeError: float() ... not 'tuple'`.
- Invoices: `invoices.py` predates the DomainError convention. `mark_paid` still raises `KeyError`/`ValueError`. Follow `DomainError` for new code, and don't change `mark_paid` unless the ticket asks. `late_fee_for` (PRC-106) follows DomainError and returns `Money`. (Earlier note said `void_invoice` existed in invoices.py; it does not in the current tree, so don't rely on it.) Invoice dates are naive UTC: see [[invoice-timestamps]].
- Refunds (PRC-105): `parcelo/refunds.py` `create_refund(invoice_id, amount)`. Unknown invoice -> `E_NOT_FOUND`, status != "paid" -> `E_BAD_STATE`. Amount stored as `Money.parse(amount)`. Audit `refund.created`. `db.refunds` dict lives in `parcelo/store.py` and is cleared in `reset()`. Tests in `tests/unit/test_refunds.py` (4 tests). CI passed and review approved on first pass. Ticket did not specify an over-refund cap or a positive-amount check; none added, and the reviewer did not ask for one. Treat them as an open question for any future refund/payment ticket, not a default requirement.
- **Ids:** always `ids.new_id("<PREFIX>")` from `parcelo/ids.py`. Never `uuid` (despite `add_customer` using it) or hand-built strings. Support tooling parses the `prefix_000001` format. See [[review-feedback-id-format-prc-109]].
- **Business constants (PRC-153 changes requested):** thresholds, limits, rates, and percentages live in `parcelo/settings.py` as UPPER_CASE constants, imported by the feature module. Never a bare number in a function body, and never a constant defined in the feature module. Finance edits that one file. See [[review-settings-constants-prc-153]]. `parcelo/settings.py` now exists (created for PRC-156, holding `HEAVY_THRESHOLD_KG` and `HEAVY_SURCHARGE_PER_KG`), so add new constants there rather than creating the file again. Check `ls parcelo/` anyway, since the tree can change between tickets. PRC-158's diff showed `parcelo/settings.py` as newly created (not present before that ticket), so the PRC-156 note above is not reliable across tickets. Always check before writing; if missing, create it with a docstring ([[returns-prc-158]]).
- Timestamps: use `clock.now()` (not `datetime.now()`) so tests can pin time with `clock.set_fixed()`.

**Rule.** Since the release tooling change, each bullet under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` is `- [PRC-123] <module>: <what changed>`. The id goes first, in square brackets. 2. Write `- [PRC-NNN] module: short description`. Nothing after the id. No parentheses at the end.

**Recurring review comment.** Both PRC-109 (`add_address`) and PRC-143 (`schedule_pickup`) got "changes requested" with the same text: "Don't build ids with `uuid` or by hand. Use `ids.new_id("<prefix>")` from `parcelo.ids`, support tooling depends on the `prefix_000001` format."

files.review-idempotent-transitions-prc-152.md:
---
name: review-idempotent-transitions-prc-152
description: Review rule (PRC-152 and PRC-157 both changes requested): a state change to the status the entity already has must return it unchanged, no error, no second event, because callers retry on timeouts. Overrides any ticket wording that seems to forbid it. Read for ANY mark/hold/cancel/void/deactivate/set-status function.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

PRC-152 (`shipments.mark_lost`) was sent back: calling it twice on the same shipment raised or re-emitted. My code only guarded `status == "delivered"`, so a second `mark_lost` on a lost shipment set status again and emitted a second `shipment.lost` event. The reviewer's rule: our callers retry on timeouts, so a transition into the target state must be idempotent.

PRC-157 (`invoices.hold_invoice`) hit the same rule again. The ticket said "only open invoices can be held", and I made a repeat hold raise `E_BAD_STATE`. The reviewer sent it back. **Lesson: when a ticket's wording seems to forbid a repeat into the target state, the ticket still does not override this rule.** The ticket's "only open" limits the source states. Repeat calls into the target state are still no-ops. If the ticket really wants an error there, say so in the final message and ask; don't pick the error silently.

Rule for every state-changing function:
1. **Already in the target state -> return the entity unchanged.** No error, no timestamp change, no event emitted. Example: `mark_lost` on a `lost` shipment returns it as-is.
2. **Target state reached from a forbidden state -> E_BAD_STATE**, as before (e.g. `delivered` cannot become `lost`).
3. **Unknown id -> E_NOT_FOUND**, checked first.
4. Put the idempotent check before the transition guard, and before any write or `events.emit`.

Test pattern for every such function (add it to the one new test file):
- Call twice. Assert the second call returns without error, status unchanged, and `len(events.OUTBOX)` did not grow on the second call (record the length after the first call and compare).
- For timestamp transitions, also assert the first timestamp did not change ([[state-transitions]]).

Why: retries are normal in this codebase. A duplicate event or a spurious error on retry is a bug, not a corner case. The reviewer named it explicitly for PRC-152.

How to apply: before coding any status change, ask "what happens if this is called twice?" If the answer is not "nothing", add the early return and the test. Do this before reading the ticket's error wording, not after. Also see [[shipment-lost-prc-152]], [[invoice-hold-prc-157]], [[state-transitions]], [[ticket-checklist]].

Fix pattern: `sorted((s for s in db.shipments.values() if s.customer_id == customer_id), key=lambda s: s.id)`. Add a test that inserts entities out of id order (or checks `[s.id for s in result] == sorted(...)`) so the order is pinned. Applies to any "list/all/find" function, not just this one.

2. **Docs (rule).** New public function -> add a bullet to `docs/api.md`, e.g. ``- `shipments.list_shipments(customer_id)`: list a customer's shipments, sorted by id``. Support tooling and the partner team read that file. Reviewer's example line was for `mark_lost`; it shows the format, not a request to add that function. Check `docs/api.md` exists and grep it for the function name before submitting.

**Why:** Reviewer flagged both as missing from a diff that otherwise passed CI. Neither was in the ticket text, so the ticket wording alone does not catch them.

**How to apply:** For any new public function, (a) grep `docs/api.md` and add a line; (b) if it returns a list of entities, sort by `id` and test the order. See [[ticket-checklist]] steps 14 and 15 and [[list-shipments-prc-151]].

---
name: review-rules-prc-103
description: Review rules from PRC-103 (CI failed + changes requested): use DomainError not ValueError, use Money not float, never import parcelo.legacy
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

PRC-103 (`quote_with_surcharge`) was sent back on three review points, plus a CI failure. I wrote the code to the ticket's wording ("must fail" -> `ValueError`) and a raw float money return. Both were wrong for this codebase.

Review rules:
1. **Errors:** new code raises `DomainError` from `parcelo.errors` with a registered `E_...` code (add one to `CODES` if nothing fits). The API layer maps those codes to responses. "Must fail" in a ticket means "raise DomainError", not `ValueError`/`KeyError`.
2. **Money:** return `Money` from `parcelo.money`. Never return a raw float for a currency amount. Wrap old float values with `Money.parse`.
3. **Legacy:** do not import from `parcelo.legacy`. It is being deleted. Reimplement the small piece you need next to the change.

CI also failed: `TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'tuple'` on three surcharge tests. The failing test names (`test_local_has_no_surcharge`, `test_national_surcharge`, `test_international_surcharge`) do not match the file I wrote (`test_local_has_zero_surcharge`, etc.), so CI ran tests I never saw. I had no pytest output in hand before submitting.

**Repeat offence (PRC-110):** the float rule was rejected again on `discounted_quote`, even though I had this file in memory. I copied the float return from the neighbouring `quote()` instead of using `Money`. Money-returning code is the default. A float return is only acceptable if the ticket and reviewer say so explicitly, and the answer is still not to copy a float helper. See [[rates-gold-discount-prc-110]].

**Repeat list on PRC-112:** the reviewer again cited audit, `clock.now()`, `ids.new_id`, and `Money`. All four were already in the submitted diff (file:line checks needed). Reviewer comments can point at code that is already correct, or be generic. Verify each one against the actual lines, then say so in the final message with file:line. Don't rewrite working code just to match the comment. CI on PRC-112 failed for a separate reason (over-strict state guard). See [[claims-prc-112]].

**Repeat offence (PRC-150):** the reviewer rejected a float write-back into `Customer.credit_limit`, even though the function returned `Money`. The float was the stored value, not the return. Money rule covers both return values and stored amounts. I had justified it with the PRC-113 precedent, which was not a safe reason. See [[customer-credit-limit-prc-150]].

**Why:** The rounding incident made money floats a banned pattern. Legacy is on a deletion schedule, so new imports from it break later. The team's error-code API depends on DomainError.

**How to apply:** Before writing any function that returns an amount, check `parcelo/money.py` and use `Money`. Before writing any `raise`, use `DomainError` with a code from `CODES`. Before importing, confirm the module is not under `parcelo/legacy`. Before reporting done, run `python -m pytest -q` and paste the actual output, and check any CI failure names against what you wrote. See [[parcelo-conventions]] and [[ticket-checklist]].
files.review-settings-constants-prc-153.md:
---
name: review-settings-constants-prc-153
description: PRC-153 review (changes requested): business thresholds/rates must be UPPER_CASE named constants in parcelo/settings.py and imported, not defined in the module or inlined. Finance changes these and wants one place. Applies to any ticket with a limit, threshold, rate, percent, or cap.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

PRC-153 (`customers.needs_review`) got CHANGES REQUESTED from code review. CI passed. The reviewer said: "There is a bare number for a business threshold/rate in the function body. Put it in `parcelo/settings.py` as a named UPPER_CASE constant and import it. Finance asks us to change these and wants one place to look."

What I submitted: `REVIEW_MAX_OPEN_INVOICES = 3` and `REVIEW_MAX_OPEN_TOTAL = Money.parse("250.00")` defined at the top of `parcelo/customers.py`. Named constants, but in the wrong file. The reviewer wants them in `parcelo/settings.py`.

**Rule:** any business number (threshold, limit, cap, rate, percent, fee, days-before-something) goes in `parcelo/settings.py` as an UPPER_CASE constant. The function imports it. It does not live in the feature module, and it is never a literal in a function body.
- Money thresholds: store as `Money.parse("250.00")` in settings, or as a string the caller parses. Compare with Money, never float.
- Keep the value the ticket states. Don't invent extra constants.
- Tests may import the same constant from `parcelo.settings` for boundary tests (e.g. `SETTING + Money.parse("0.01")`). Don't hard-code 250 in tests either if you can import it. Hard-coding in tests is acceptable only if the reviewer hasn't objected.

**Why:** Finance changes these numbers and wants one file to edit. A constant in a feature module is still a second place to look.

**How to apply:** Before writing a function with a comparison against a number that comes from the ticket, grep `parcelo/settings.py`. If it exists, add there. If it doesn't exist in the tree, check first (`ls parcelo/`); create it with a module docstring and the new constants, then import. Say in the final message that you created it. Check `parcelo/legacy/` only as a reference for the value. Never import from it (see [[review-rules-prc-103]]).

Related: [[needs-review-prc-153]], [[parcelo-conventions]], [[ticket-checklist]] (step 17).
